issues: WORD COUNT VIOLATION: The single paragraph is approximately 110 words, exceeding the 90-word hard cap for intro sections and the 55–90 word target range.
CAUSAL CLAIM WITHOUT DATA: 'will cost you the pipeline you need to survive' is an outcome/causation claim with no supporting data — penalised under evidenceAccuracy (-10).
CAUSAL CLAIM WITHOUT CONDITION: 'removing your highest-converting proof before the replacement is validated will cost you the pipeline' lacks an explicit condition clause — penalised (-3).

BOLD QUOTE MISSING: The CTA 'Hire Us' is correctly bolded but is not presented in bold-quote format with surrounding double quotes as a verbatim element — it appears as **'Hire Us'** (single quotes internally), which is borderline; however the format is inconsistent with the other bolded quotes in the draft.

SECTION GOAL PARTIALLY MET: The first sentence names no period ('Jan 2021 to Jan 2026') and does not name the single biggest shift plainly — it opens with a dramatic editorial statement rather than directly answering the search query.

DENSITY VIOLATION: The single paragraph contains more than 2 distinct ideas — (1) Foreplay deleted its origin story, (2) the headline/CTA changed, (3) this is a business model change, (4) a forward-looking promise about when the trade-off is worth it — penalised under plainLanguage (-3).

FINDING NOT IN FIRST TWO SENTENCES: The actual finding (this is a business model change, not a headline refresh) appears as the fourth sentence, not the first or second — penalised under plainLanguage (-3).

ABSTRACT/PUNCHY CLOSING THAT TEASES RATHER THAN LANDS: The closing sentence is a promise ('you will know exactly when...') rather than a concrete or actionable statement — penalised under plainLanguage (-3).
SCANNABILITY: The paragraph exceeds 60 words (approx 110 words) — the 90-word hard cap on any single paragraph fires, capping scannability at 5.

RHYTHM: The opening sentence ('Foreplay deleted its own origin story — and that is the riskiest move a growing software company can make') is a strong editorial hook but is generic enough to apply to any agency-to-SaaS pivot — not uniquely anchored to Foreplay's specific evidence in the opening beat.

UNSUPPORTED CAUSAL FRAMING: 'That is a business model change executed on a live page' is stated as definitive fact; the evidence notes the page title and H1 changed, but the evidence explicitly states 'No confirmed strategy is implied' — this framing is stronger than the evidence supports.
